name: FEG SmartBridge relayer whitelists forged Wormhole source on superAdmin payload
summary: FEG's unverified relayer whitelists a Wormhole message's source address whenever the payload's user is a superAdmin, so any contract can make itself a trusted source. The attacker sent such a message naming the FEG admin, then a second one that made SmartBridge.registerWithdraw credit it, and withdrew and sold nearly all bridged FEG on BSC, Base and Ethereum.
notes: The reset is the SmartBridge deployment, which registered the bridge for FEG in DataReader (bridgeSD) and fixed its relayer; the relayer resolves the bridge through that entry. Later relayer admin calls set fees, gas and peers, which the exploited path does not read. The relayer runs the same code at the same address on Base and Ethereum.
BSC delivered the first forged message. Later forged messages by 0xb1e2afdb and 0x2218666f registered withdrawals but moved no FEG, so they are not campaign.

FEG is valued at the native currency its sales drew from FEG pools on each chain (rule 15): the released quantities far exceed market depth, so DefiLlama quotes would overstate the loss about fiftyfold.
